scope: Studio-approved design references; not production shipped status

D01.behavior: Open the Chat Train tab in Studio. Native placement commands remain owned by the existing agent portal contract; this review adds no production command.

D02.behavior: Sending leaves the composer available at the active tail. It does not create a second run while a response is active.

D03.behavior: Idle → static selection or drag; output click → unsent continuation; historical output drag or Fork → branch; send → responding; Stop → retained partial reply. S01, S05.

D04.behavior: Movement exceeding 4 screen pixels is a drag. An unselected body drag moves the card. A stationary click selects it; a subsequent text drag selects text. Controls retain their own actions.

D05.behavior: Enter sends; Shift+Enter inserts a newline. Middle drag, right drag, or Space+left drag pans. Wheel zooms; Shift+wheel pans horizontally. Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo/redo. Selected overflowing text consumes scrolling; the single window scrolls under its pointer.

D06.behavior: No new grid, ortho, or object-snap behavior is introduced by this Studio review. Keep production snapping with its existing owner.

D07.behavior: Horizontal resizing fixes width and derives height from that width. Explicit vertical resizing may retain an authored height. Full expansion releases the height limit but keeps width. S04.

D08.behavior: Typing edits the composer or an explicitly opened name/key field. No numeric geometry entry is introduced.

D09.behavior: Resize preview recomputes text/composer bounds from the current width on every frame. Responding and estimated count replace the model label during a run; Stop replaces the output dot. S03, S04.

D10.behavior: Unselected text body uses grab/move behavior; selected text uses text selection; edge cursors identify resize direction. Small interactive controls retain pointer feedback.

D11.behavior: Card moves, resize, layout changes, folds, agent choices, and deletion are reversible model actions. One drag commits once. Streaming bytes and per-keystroke draft edits are not individual undo steps.

D12.behavior: Escape closes transient menus/dialogs or cancels a live pointer gesture. Cancellation preserves the composer and returns geometry to its pre-gesture state. Apply the production cancel stack when implementing natively.

D13.behavior: Selection enables text highlighting after the stationary selection click. It does not add a competing toolbar or message bubble. Header and edge controls stay in place.

D14.behavior: Rename inline, adjust settings from the header, resize at edges, and reflow through the presentation menu. A chosen width survives fold/reopen and reload.

D15.behavior: This lock covers Chat Train and the reusable Studio workflow. It does not claim live provider connections, credential storage, scheduled execution, production permission grants, or native renderer pixel identity.

D16.behavior: Preserve the native light/dark palette, Ubuntu font, compact header, plain text and connected-card presentation. Global theme changes do not rewrite conversation content.

D17.behavior: Card control, edge, body, and text-selection hit regions have separate owners. Fold SVGs cannot intercept the neighboring fold hit target. History rails are derived, not removable context wires.

D18.behavior: The production agent is a host portal; inherit the existing portal authority boundary. The Studio is a local simulation and does not grant host authority.

D19.behavior: Conversation order is the canonical turn tree. Cards are views over stable turn IDs. Additional source context remains explicit; this Studio adds no hidden canvas context.

D20.behavior: Provider, model, effort, and speed are separate fields. Allowed choices come from one model capability catalogue and are validated again for the submitted turn. S02.

D21.behavior: Only an explicit send begins a reply. Changing presentation, opening menus, configuring an agent, or creating an unsent branch never begins inference.

D22.behavior: S01 governs compact menus; S03 governs scrollbar/text treatment; S05 governs selection and dragging. Composer remains independently editable.

D23.behavior: World-space card/text geometry scales with canvas zoom without rewrapping because of zoom alone. Menus remain screen-sized. Long labels truncate, not expand the card. S06.

D24.behavior: n/a to this local preview. The standalone Markdown contract and readable viewer are review artifacts, not exported live agent behavior.

D25.behavior: n/a: this session adds no bake operation.

D26.behavior: Local Studio conversation and notes survive reload. Provider-key status is shared across Studio instances; secret text is not stored. Production collaboration stays with its canonical journal/source owners.

D27.behavior: Use the existing production agent/command surface when porting. No new hidden agent permission or tool is authorized by a Studio control.

D28.behavior: Baseline font/tokens and renderer provenance are pinned in chat-train/BASELINE.md. The sample model catalogue and long conversation are deterministic fixtures, not availability promises.

D29.behavior: A live resize never accumulates prior-frame clipping offsets. Streaming cannot replace an active resize preview. The normal single window is height-bounded; Full conversation explicitly exposes all text.

D30.behavior: Unsupported settings stay visible but disabled and explain why on hover. Invalid settings normalize to an allowed model value before send. Stop keeps received text. An expired/missing key always has a reachable Add/Change route.

D31.behavior: Canonical messages/branches, model choices, authored width, fold, and drafts persist. Camera, hover, scrollbar fade, and stream animation are view state. Presentation changes retain draft identity and history.

D32.behavior: API-key entry is a dedicated masked field reached through its own provider-row chevron. In Studio, only sample status is retained; real integration must use the existing secure credential owner. Access and schedule controls remain simulations here.

D33.behavior: Header: status dot, title, selected model/effort/speed feedback, fold control, ellipsis, output/Stop. S01/S06. The action menu uses separate presentation, Full conversation, action, and sizing/deletion sections.

D34.behavior: Single chat window combines each linear conversation path into one scrollable card with a pinned composer. Branch topology remains explicit. Full conversation means fit all card text, not remove pair formatting or open a different transcript.

D35.behavior: Provider configuration, fold, text, and composer belong to their card. Studio tabs, Debrief, native reference and review notes remain outside the element canvas. S07.

changes.title: One element per Studio tab
changes.behavior: Chat Train is the first, persistent primary tab. Future reviews start in their own isolated canvas tab.

changes.title: Remove invented enclosing chrome
changes.behavior: Cards sit directly on the canvas. No giant outer conversation frame, role bubbles, or modality dashboard surrounds them.

changes.title: Four independent agent settings
changes.behavior: Provider, Model, Effort, and Speed are distinct compact rows.

changes.title: Anchored submenus
changes.behavior: The clicked header keeps its icon, label and selected value on the same datum. Options replace lower rows; the same chevron closes it. No Back row.

changes.title: Shared menu width
changes.behavior: Picker pages use the chat ellipsis menu width, not a wide settings panel. Explanations appear on hover.

changes.title: Provider identities
changes.behavior: Use existing Cursor and Codex/OpenAI catalogue marks where available; Local may use a generic computer mark.

changes.title: Dedicated API-key route
changes.behavior: The API provider has a separate key chevron and explicit Add/Change key action with a masked input. Selecting a provider does not open the key editor or send a request.

changes.title: Model capability rubric
changes.behavior: Each model declares effort and speed options. Omitted capability arrays are invalid; empty arrays mean unsupported. No unavailable option is shown as selectable.

changes.title: Header selection feedback
changes.behavior: Show a muted effort label beside the selected model. Standard has no lightning bolt, Fast one complete bolt, Ultra two complete bolts. Other speed metadata is explicit.

changes.title: Long-name containment
changes.behavior: A deliberately oversized model name elides in header and menus, remains complete in the stored selection and hover help, and cannot push effort/chevrons off the card.

changes.title: Readable single window
changes.behavior: Use a wider plain-text window, visible user/agent distinction by indent/ink, and one pinned composer. Preserve history, branches and drafts across layout changes.

changes.title: Transient scroll thumb
changes.behavior: No permanent scrollbar gutter. An overlay thumb appears during scrolling and fades after scrolling stops; text column geometry does not change.

changes.title: Width-driven height
changes.behavior: Horizontal resize derives height from current wrapped text and recomputes transcript/composer bounds every frame. It does not accumulate clipping offsets.

changes.title: Remember authored width
changes.behavior: Collapsing and reopening retain width and appropriate height policy. Fit to text is the explicit sizing reset.

changes.title: Full conversation semantics
changes.behavior: Fit every line within the card, bypassing manual/normal scroll height limits. Preserve width and the message-pair divider. It is equivalent in intent to full expansion.

changes.title: Menu section grouping
changes.behavior: Presentation choices have their own section; Full conversation has its own section; Fork/Full access/Schedule form the next section; fitting/deletion follow.

changes.title: Menu parity
changes.behavior: Upstream, terminal and draft cards expose the same section vocabulary. Invalid actions are disabled with a reason rather than silently absent. Delete remains leaf-only.

changes.title: Drag-first body interaction
changes.behavior: An unselected card can be dragged by its text/body. A stationary click selects it; text highlighting is available on the following text gesture.

changes.title: Reliable fold hit regions
changes.behavior: Single and double fold actions own separate hit regions. Painted glyphs do not intercept the neighboring target.

changes.title: Long review fixture
changes.behavior: Three substantial message/reply pairs exercise full/partial/collapsed states and single-window scrolling.

changes.title: State reliability
changes.behavior: Unsent text, next-turn settings and branch identity survive rechunking and reload. Historical messages retain their captured settings.

changes.title: Live-resize/run isolation
changes.behavior: Streaming and camera handling cannot destroy a live geometry preview. Stop preserves partial output.

changes.title: Durable debrief
changes.behavior: Each reviewed element has a standalone contract with agreed behavior, constants, tests, preserved baseline, and dated changes. It is the parity reference for later elements.
